questions.title: Does every Collatz orbit reach 1?
questions.question: Starting from any positive integer, repeatedly halve even values and replace odd values n by 3n + 1. Must the orbit eventually reach 1?
questions.connection: Integer iteration, recurrence relations and termination proofs.
questions.gap: The source records the universal termination question as open; finite computations do not settle it.

questions.title: Are there infinitely many Mersenne primes?
questions.question: Are there infinitely many prime exponents p for which 2^p - 1 is prime?
questions.connection: Prime structure, divisibility and arithmetic sequences.
questions.gap: OEIS records infinitude as unproved; primality certificates for individual terms do not establish infinitude.

questions.title: Does a divergent reciprocal sum force long arithmetic progressions?
questions.question: If a set A of positive integers has a divergent sum of reciprocals, must it contain arithmetic progressions of every finite length?
questions.connection: Additive structure, density bounds and sum-free sets.
questions.gap: The full conjecture remains open. Bloom and Sisask proved the three-term case in 2020; that does not settle arbitrary lengths.

questions.title: Can covering systems have arbitrarily large minimum modulus?
questions.question: Can a finite covering of the integers by residue classes with distinct moduli have an arbitrarily large smallest modulus?
questions.connection: Congruences, covering systems and explicit arithmetic bounds.
questions.gap: The original question was answered negatively by Hough. The source records a lower bound of 42 and an upper bound of 616000 for the largest possible minimum modulus.
